The superlattice supports toroidal dipole (TD) and magnetic dipole (MD) resonances via intra-cluster coupling (localized) and lattice resonance (nonlocal), respectively. By tuning the pillar geometry, we achieve TD-MD coupling that enhances a TD-dominated THG response. The TD branch exhibits nearly flat dispersion over the investigated in-plane wavevector range, suggesting potential benefits for pump-resonance matching under focused-beam excitation. In particular, the TD resonance yields a nonlinear enhancement two orders of magnitude higher than the MD resonance. …

articles.authors: Leandro Risso Venancio, Jonathan Dong, Jacopo Bertolotti, Mickael Mounaix
articles.summary: With the exponential growth in demand for computing power, photonics offers a sustainable and competitive alternative to conventional electronic computing. In this article, we present how wavefront shaping, by means of a spatial light modulator, provides a versatile platform for optical computing. Using only linear optical components, we introduce an approach that exploits structural nonlinearity to enhance the forecasting of a chaotic time series.

articles.title: Seeing deeper with dynamic wavefront shaping in optical microscopy
articles.authors: Julian Malobert, Juan Muñoz-Bolaños, Eva Ernst, Simon Moser, Alexander Jesacher
articles.summary: Optical microscopy is indispensable in biology andmedicine. However, tissue scatters the imaging light, which limits how deeply and clearly it can see. Adaptive optics uses dynamic wavefront shaping to compensate for aberrations induced by the sample and can increase imaging depth. We demonstrate this principle using three complementary techniques: multi-photon microscopy for deep imaging, confocal Raman microscopy for label-free chemical contrast and single-molecule localisation microscopy for nanometre-scale imaging.

articles.title: Spatial shaping of ultrafast laser beams for advanced material processing
articles.authors: Cyril Mauclair
articles.summary: Ultrafast lasers enable material processing with remarkable precision, but exploiting the increasing power of modern laser sources remains challenging. Dynamic wavefront shaping offers a powerful solution by tailoring the focal intensity distribution in space. This article introduces the main concepts and technologies behind spatial beam shaping and illustrates how shaped beams, parallel processing and structured light can improve the flexibility and efficiency of laser processing.

To address these challenges, this study proposes a tunable needle-like beam (NLB) generation method based on a tunable aberration unit (TAU). By inserting the TAU into the sample arm of an existing OCT system, tunable spherical aberration is introduced. …

We exploit this anisotropy by foveating the input basis: small angles are sampled finely and large angles are grouped into coarser modes, so that each mode carries a similar share of the transmitted light at a fixed total number of modes. …

articles.title: Fourier pixels: unifying bidirectional vectorial light-field generation and sensing at the microscale
articles.authors: Haofan Huang, Zechen Wei, Puxiang Lai
articles.summary: This commentary highlights Fourier pixels, a recent advance in planar optics that enables continuous momentum space engineering and full vectorial light-field manipulation. By replacing discrete resonators with continuous surface topographies, Fourier pixels overcome the near-field coupling and phase discretization limits of classical metasurfaces, providing an alternative route to monolithic on-chip optical processing. They unify light generation and sensing in a single micrometer-scale pixel, enabling simultaneous, bidirectional control of amplitude, phase, and polarization. We discuss the principles, demonstrations, and challenges toward practical on-chip photonic technologies.
